questions.prompt: Explain the roles of UIViewRepresentable and UIHostingController when connecting SwiftUI and UIKit. Answer in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that UIViewRepresentable wraps UIKit views for use in SwiftUI
Explains that UIHostingController embeds SwiftUI views inside UIKit view controller hierarchies

questions.modelAnswer: UIViewRepresentable wraps native UIKit views so developers can use them inside SwiftUI view hierarchies. In the opposite direction, UIHostingController embeds SwiftUI views inside UIKit view controller hierarchies. Together, they allow teams to migrate screens incrementally between both frameworks.

questions.prompt: Explain the purpose of makeCoordinator and how the Coordinator communicates events back to SwiftUI. Answer in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that makeCoordinator instantiates a helper object to act as delegate or target for UIKit
Explains that the Coordinator updates SwiftUI state or bindings when UIKit events occur

questions.modelAnswer: The makeCoordinator method creates a custom Coordinator instance before makeUIView runs. The Coordinator acts as the UIKit delegate or target-action responder for user events. When the user interacts with the UIKit view, the Coordinator mutates a SwiftUI binding or state variable to keep the frameworks in sync.

questions.prompt: Describe two common traps when using UIViewRepresentable and how to avoid them. Answer in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Identifies creating new views inside updateUIView and explains to create them once in makeUIView
Identifies mutating SwiftUI state directly inside updateUIView causing recursion

questions.modelAnswer: One common trap is creating new UIKit views inside updateUIView, which resets view state and hurts performance; views should be created once in makeUIView. Another trap is mutating SwiftUI state directly inside updateUIView, which triggers recursive update cycles. Developers should only mutate SwiftUI state from the Coordinator in response to user actions.

questions.prompt: How do you properly embed a UIHostingController inside a UIKit UIViewController? Answer in 2 to 5 sentences.
questions.lessonSection: How to answer in the interview

rubric.criterion: Mentions calling addChild to establish parent-child view controller relationship
Mentions adding the hosting controller view with addSubview and setting layout
Mentions calling didMove(toParent:) to complete containment ceremony

questions.modelAnswer: To embed a UIHostingController, you first call addChild to establish the parent-child relationship. Next, you add the hosting controller's view to the view hierarchy using addSubview and configure layout constraints. Finally, you call didMove(toParent: self) so the hosting controller receives proper lifecycle callbacks and safe area updates.

questions.prompt: What is UIHostingConfiguration, and what advantage does it offer over embedding individual hosting controllers in cells? Answer in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that UIHostingConfiguration allows using SwiftUI views inside collection and table view cells on iOS 16+
Explains that it avoids manual UIHostingController containment ceremony and view hierarchy overhead

questions.modelAnswer: Introduced in iOS 16, UIHostingConfiguration allows developers to configure collection view and table view cells using SwiftUI views. It eliminates the boilerplate of manually managing child UIHostingController instances inside reusable cells. This reduces view controller hierarchy overhead and improves scrolling performance.
